title: A Comparative Evaluation of Modbus Security Telemetry Extraction.
abstract: Network security frequently treats packet captures as ground truth, although most detection and analysis pipelines operate on structured telemetry produced by protocol parsers rather than directly on packet bytes. This study evaluates how parser selection affects Modbus telemetry by processing an identical controlled traffic with Suricata, TShark, and Zeek. Their outputs are compared in terms of output structure, protocol-field fidelity, payload visibility, transaction reconstruction, exception representation, and timing observability. The results show differences in both record structure and analytical content. Consequently, the selected parser determines which features are directly available for detection engineering, behavioral analysis, SIEM integration, dataset construction, and machine-learning applications. These findings show that protocol parsing is not a neutral preprocessing step. Even with identical packet-level input, parser implementation and configuration can alter the structure, completeness, and semantics of the resulting cybersecurity dataset. Reproducible industrial cybersecurity research should therefore document and validate the parsing stage and use cross-parser verification when feasible.

title: Federated Transfer Learning with Attentional Graph Neural Networks for Zero-Day IoT Botnet Detection and Secure Edge Orchestration.
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) devices are increasingly appearing in a wide variety of edge environments, and these environments have become cybersecurity hot spots due to the increased vulnerability of them to sophisticated Zero-Day botnets propagation and Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks. However, traditional centralized intrusion detection system (IDS) is not capable of dealing with privacy constraints, communication overhead and dynamic topological structures of modern IoT networks. To solve these problems, a novel federated transfer learning framework, with the support of Attentional Graph Neural Networks (AGNN) is proposed for decentralized zero-day botnet detection at resource-constrained edge nodes. Proposed architecture includes federated learning to achieve collaborative model training, without sharing raw telemetry data and graph-based spatial modeling for capturing complex inter-device communication anomalies. Moreover, a transfer learning mechanism fine-tunes pre-trained threat intelligence on newly emerging edge sub-networks with limited fine-tuning. Empirical results on the benchmark IoT intrusion datasets (N-BaIoT and BoT-IoT) show a detection accuracy of 98.6%, 0.97 in ROC-AUC, a reduction of false alarm rate to 0.42% and a reduction of communication bandwidth overhead of 45.3% when compared to the traditional centralized deep learning paradigms. The results of ablation experiments indicate that the base GNN, the base GNN with attention and the base GNN with federated attention, together with the full transfer-learning setup, gradually improves the ablation results.

title: RAMP: History-Aware Multi-Access Path Management for Resilient Edge Networks.
abstract: Multi-access connectivity can improve the resilience of mission-critical edge services by allowing traffic to migrate across heterogeneous network paths. However, conventional path-selection policies typically react to current availability or measured performance. In recurrently unstable networks, a degraded path may briefly appear healthy and attract traffic again before its condition has stabilized. Such premature path reuse can cause repeated path migration, tail-latency spikes, and deadline violations. This paper presents RAMP, a lightweight history-aware multi-access path-management policy designed for recurrent network degradation and recovery. RAMP combines exponentially smoothed round-trip-time (RTT) measurements with short-term indicators of instability, including recent failures, consecutive failures, and latency variability. Recently unstable paths therefore retain a temporary risk penalty even after their instantaneous latency improves. We evaluate RAMP against single-path operation, reactive failover, minimum-RTT selection, and a hysteresis-based RTT baseline across five controlled network conditions. The evaluation comprises 75 independent 60-second runs and 9,000 application transactions. Under recurrent degradation and recovery, RAMP achieves 99.72% deadline satisfaction, compared with 98.61% for MinRTT and 94.44% for hysteresis-based RTT selection. RAMP reduces scheduler switches from six to two and Resilience Debt from 3.33 s to 0.17 s relative to the hysteresis baseline. Under bursty impairment, RAMP again reaches 99.72% deadline satisfaction and 0.17 s Resilience Debt. Conversely, under stable, monotonic-degradation, and hard-failure conditions, its advantage is small or absent. The results show that short-term instability memory is particularly useful under recurrent non-stationary impairment, where instantaneous path quality can encourage premature path reuse.

title: Toward Edge-Assisted Live Synthesis of 3D Digital Twins in 6G.
abstract: Live synthesis of 3D digital twins from vehicle-mounted and roadside camera streams could provide timely, spatially rich representations of urban environments. However, constructing radiance-field models from distributed camera streams with short processing delays introduces substantial computation, coordination, and localization requirements. This paper presents a controlled measurement study of centralized, distributed, and federated radiance-field synthesis under prospective 6G edge-cloud assumptions. Using a CARLA-based vehicular scenario, we show that centralized model training can reach the target reconstruction quality in under 2 minutes under favorable configurations, excluding data transfer and method-specific preprocessing. Distributed and federated approaches spread the training workload across edge nodes: Mega-NeRF enables fast model merging but achieves lower quality than centralized Nerfacto, whereas Fed3DGS approaches centralized Splatfacto quality on guided trajectories but becomes aggregation-bound. Moderate camera-position errors cause limited degradation, whereas multi-meter errors substantially reduce reconstruction quality. These results identify faster model synthesis, efficient aggregation, coverage-aware data acquisition, and accurate localization as key requirements for scalable live synthesis of 3D digital twins.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: PRISM: Reinforced Semantic Communication for Decentralized Federated Anomaly Detection in Vehicular Networks.
abstract: Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) enables collaborative learning that preserves privacy, but faces critical communication challenges in bandwidth-constrained environments such as vehicular networks. We propose Policy-driven Representation and Information Selection Method (PRISM), a Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based method that optimizes semantic communication in DFL through adaptive representation selection and intelligent topology management. Our dual-model architecture separates task learning (autoencoder-based anomaly detection) from communication control (Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based decision making), enabling agents to dynamically select between transmitting full model weights or compressed trajectory embeddings. We formulate this as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) and train using a Centralized Training Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm. We demonstrate our method through a digital twin monitoring scenario where vehicles collaboratively detect trajectory anomalies in neighbors' behavior in real time, and the logged detections support forensic analysis, insurance claims, and fleet auditing. Experiments on Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO) generated Barcelona traffic data show an F1-score of 0.90, scaling from 2 to 128 agents with graceful degradation past N = 32, Byzantine-robust aggregation, and validation on Next Generation Simulation (NGSIM) US-101 real traces (F1 0.82). The learned policy exhibits emergent temporal behavior: transmitting weights early during training when model divergence is high, then shifting to embeddings as models converge, with the weight-to-embedding mix derived as the equilibrium of the communication budget constraint. The method generalizes to other bandwidth-limited collaborative learning domains.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: METRO: MAP-Enhanced Twin Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning-Based Coverage and Capacity Optimization.
abstract: Few-shot coverage and capacity optimization (CCO) under a small adjustment budget is challenging: model-based methods suffer from simulator mismatch, while feedback-based methods are sample-starved. We address this challenge with a rollout-based policy-improvement framework. Rather than deploying the trained policy's highest-probability action directly, we use the policy as a proposal mechanism and a maximum a posteriori (MAP)-calibrated digital twin (DT) as the evaluator. The policy samples candidate actions; each is simulated for multiple steps inside the twin, and only the highest-return candidate is deployed. Sparse measurements report signal strength and quality but not user-equipment (UE) locations; we therefore estimate UE locations by MAP inference using DT-predicted measurements as likelihoods and recalibrate the DT to the current network state at each step. Three trainingside components strengthen the candidate generation: a Heaviside reward for safety, a recurrent network for partial observability, and domain randomization for simulator mismatch. Ablation studies validate these components. Under a 10-shot emulated-field budget, METRO achieves a lower violation rate than classical simulated annealing and gains comparable to a 50×-budget baseline.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Optimal Parallel Scheduling under Concave Speedup Functions.
abstract: Efficiently scheduling parallel computing resources across multiple concurrent jobs is a core challenge in modern cloud and edge computing systems that support AI-driven applications. Allocating more resources to a job accelerates its completion, but with diminishing returns. Prior work (heSRPT) has solved this problem for certain speedup functions with an exponential form, providing a closed-form solution. However, the general case with arbitrary concave speedup functions—which more accurately capture real-world workloads—has remained open. In this paper, we solve this open problem by developing optimal scheduling algorithms for parallel jobs under general concave speedup functions. We first discover a fundamental and broadly-applicable rule for optimal parallel scheduling, namely the Consistent Derivative Ratio (CDR) Rule , which states that the ratio of the derivatives of the speedup functions across active jobs remains constant over time. To efficiently compute the optimal allocations that satisfy the CDR Rule, we propose the General Water-Filling (GWF) method, a more general version of classical water-filling in wireless communications. Combining these insights, we design the SmartFill Algorithm to solve the general scheduling problem. Unlike heSRPT, which always allocates resources to all active jobs, SmartFill selectively determines which jobs should receive resources and how much they should be allocated. For a broad class of so-called regular speedup functions, SmartFill yields closed-form optimal solutions, while for non-regular functions it efficiently computes the optimum numerically. Simulation results show that SmartFill can outperform heSRPT across a wide range of concave speedup functions.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: POLAR: Online Learning for LoRA Adapter Caching and Routing in Edge LLM Serving.
abstract: Edge deployment of large language models (LLMs) increasingly relies on libraries of lightweight LoRA adapters, yet GPU/DRAM can keep only a small resident subset at a time. Serving a request through a non-resident adapter requires paging its weights from storage, incurring measurable latency. This creates a two-timescale online control problem: on a slow timescale, the system selects which adapters remain resident in fast memory, while on a fast timescale it routes each request to an adapter whose context-dependent utility is unknown a priori. The two decisions are tightly coupled: the cache determines the cost of exploration, and the router determines which adapters receive informative feedback. We formulate this joint caching-and-routing problem as a two-timescale contextual bandit and propose POLAR (Paging and Online Learning for Adapter Routing). POLAR pairs a cache-aware LinUCB router with an epoch-based cache controller. We study two variants. A fixed-epoch version provides a robust baseline with worst-case regret guarantees under arbitrary contexts. An epoch-doubling version, POLAR+, adds forced exploration and improved cache optimization to achieve O~(dNT+KT) sublinear regret under stochastic regularity and cacheability conditions, where N is the adapter count, K the cache size, d the context dimension, and T the horizon. The routing term matches the standard contextual-bandit rate up to logarithmic factors, showing that the memory hierarchy does not fundamentally slow routing learning. Experiments using 15 real LoRA adapters for Qwen2.5-7B together with measured GPU paging latencies show that adaptive cache control substantially outperforms heuristic caching baselines.

title: Demo: Closed-Loop Sionna-Isaac Sim Co-Simulation Framework for Wireless-Aware Robot Navigation over ROS 2.
abstract: A robot that offloads its control loop to the network carries the receiver with it, so link quality is decided by where it goes. Simulating this requires both a physics engine and a site-specific propagation model at once; to our knowledge no simulator natively unifies both, with existing couplings of the two limited to offline analyses. We demonstrate a real-time co-simulation framework coupling NVIDIA Isaac Sim and NVIDIA Sionna over ROS 2 that closes the perception-action-communication (PAC) loop between them. Sionna ray-traces the base-station-to-robot channel over the exact geometry Isaac Sim simulates on—rather than modeling it stochastically—and feeds channel states back into the control loop in real time. Ray-traced on GPU, the coverage map is refreshed in ~16 ms (~60 Hz), fast enough for real-time control. To showcase the framework's utility, we implement a wireless-aware navigation application in an OpenStreetMap(OSM)-derived SUTD campus twin with two Nova Carter robots: the closed-loop planner eliminates communication outage at only +7.4% traversal time over the shortest-path baseline (which spends 7.9 s of its 81.2 s run disconnected).

title: Distributed Collaborative Positioning through ISAC for GPS-Denied Robotic Swarms.
abstract: Robotic swarms in GPS-denied environments require accurate position and velocity in real-time for all nodes, without external infrastructure or centralized control. Existing positioning approaches, including collaborative positioning, fail because of non-scalable (O(N2)) measurement overhead or centralized architectures that cannot keep pace with high-mobility swarms. We present DiCoP, a novel paradigm of Distributed Collaborative Positioning through asynchronous, multi-static ISAC. Each node broadcasts a lightweight ISAC waveform, enabling all neighbors to passively and asynchronously measure relative distances and Doppler shifts through a novel differential sensing technique that cancels clock and channel frequency offsets with only O(1) overhead. Coupled with a novel joint distance-velocity localization, each node independently estimates its position and velocity, alleviating topology rigidity requirements of conventional distance-based methods. A sensing-aware distributed MAC further prioritizes measurements from fast-moving, under-measured nodes to accelerate convergence. Evaluated on our UGV swarm prototype, as well as NS3 simulations for large-scale UAV swarms (up to 100 UAVs at 15 m/s), DiCoP achieves sub-2 m error for over 89.38% of estimates, 0.062 m/s velocity error, and 54.3 ms convergence time, outperforming GPS, IMU, WiFi FTM, and centralized baselines while maintaining stable accuracy over extended mission duration.

title: Learning When to Update: A Near-Optimal Timing Bandit Approach.
abstract: Systems operating in dynamic environments require timely updates to sustain performance. For resource-intensive systems such as machine learning models and digital twins, strategically timing updates is essential. Updating too frequently wastes resources, while updating too infrequently leads to costly performance degradation. The problem is particularly challenging when the system's degradation pattern is unknown a priori, as is common in new operating environments. We formalize this challenge as a novel timing bandit problem, where each arm represents a candidate update interval with a fixed update cost and an unknown, stochastic degradation cost. Three structural properties distinguish this setting from standard multi-armed bandits: selecting an interval commits the learner to multiple time slots before the next update; arm costs are composed of per-step degradation costs and a fixed update cost; and selecting a longer interval naturally reveals degradation at every intermediate step, providing consecutive feedback relevant to shorter intervals. By exploiting these structures, we develop Balanced Consecutive Arm Elimination (BCAE). BCAE achieves O~(T) regret, improving upon the Ω~(KT) regret of standard bandit algorithms in this setting, where K is the number of candidate update intervals. We further propose an Optimism-Enhanced variant (OE-BCAE) that integrates lower-confidence-bound principles to improve empirical adaptivity while preserving the same regret order. Moreover, the regret bound achieved by our algorithms matches the theoretical lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Simulation results demonstrate that our algorithms achieve low regret and remain stable as both the number of arms and the update cost vary.

title: Receiver-Aware Token Routing for Semantic Communication.
abstract: Mission-critical mobile networks increasingly support AI-enabled services under heterogeneous and degraded wireless conditions. Semantic communication offers a promising approach by transmitting compact task-relevant representations, but most existing methods remain receiver-agnostic. We propose a receiver-aware semantic routing framework that combines hard receiver-conditioned token gating with learned mixture-of-experts transformation. A shared Vision Transformer extracts patch-level tokens, while a receiver-conditioned router jointly produces token-selection scores and expert-routing logits. Hard Top-K gating determines which routed token representations contribute to semantic aggregation, and soft expert routing adapts token representations to the receiver profile. Experiments on the MS COCO multi-label recognition task under high-SNR, low-SNR, and constrained token-retention conditions show consistent gains over static conditioning, random token selection, and pruning baselines. The results demonstrate that jointly controlling token retention and receiver-aware semantic transformation improves semantic inference under the evaluated AWGN and token-retention conditions.

A shared Vision Transformer extracts patch-level tokens, while a receiver-conditioned router jointly produces token-selection scores and expert-routing logits. Experiments on the MS COCO multi-label recognition task under high-SNR, low-SNR, and constrained token-retention conditions show consistent gains over static conditioning, random token selection, and pruning baselines. The results demonstrate that jointly controlling token retention and receiver-aware semantic transformation improves semantic inference under the evaluated AWGN and token-retention conditions.

title: Decision-Focused Learning for Bidding Optimization in Online Advertising.
abstract: In large-scale networked systems such as online marketplaces and advertising exchanges, real-time decision-making under dynamic environments is a fundamental challenge. A widely adopted paradigm is the predict-then-optimize workflow, where the prediction stage estimates key factors for decisions, and the optimization stage optimizes objectives based on these factors. However, existing prediction models are typically trained only for prediction accuracy, without awareness of the downstream optimization objective, leading to suboptimal results. We investigate this problem in the context of first-price auction bidding, a canonical decision problem in networked platforms. Specifically, we first propose the Decision-Focused Bidding (DFB) approach, which retains the predict-then-optimize workflow, but integrates the downstream objective into the training of the prediction model. To overcome the zero-gradient issue in back-propagation, we develop a smoothed decision mapping that provides usable gradients while preserving clear interpretability in the bidding context. We further show that DFB's decision-learning objective and the classical objective of learning winning probabilities are complementary under non-i.i.d. environments, and accordingly propose Enhanced DFB (EDFB), which jointly optimizes both objectives to achieve robust generalization in real-world bidding environments. Finally, our EDFB approach has been deployed in a production auto-bidding system, where it achieves a 2.3% GMV lift in a 3-day online A/B test over about 100 billion requests.

title: Query-Aware Temporal Evidence Prefetching to Support Communication-Efficient Video AIoT Reasoning.
abstract: Video Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) systems increasingly use vision-language models (VLMs) to answer questions about dynamic scenes, yet continuous high-resolution streaming may exceed wireless and latency budgets. We therefore study a layered setting in which the receiver always holds a low-resolution stream and requests only a limited number of high-resolution enhancement patches. Within this setting, we propose query-aware temporal semantic prefetching (QTPF), which uses the task query and prior low-resolution images to predict evidence locations in the next sampled observation before it arrives. On 14,913 LingoQA scenery questions, QTPF obtains 0.6355 Recall@5 under an OpenCLIP evidence target, compared with 0.5858 for a query-only learned model and 0.6270 for an independently trained query-aware last-frame predictor. The advantage persists under independently generated SigLIP targets, where QTPF obtains 0.5473 against 0.5328 for the last-frame predictor. With five enhancement patches, the delivered JPEG payload averages 9.77 KB, which is 20.9% below the 12.35 KB full-resolution image, and the predictor adds only 0.75 ms on an RTX 6000 Ada GPU.

title: Reusable Resource Allocation under Adversarial Arrivals: Learning with Delayed Feedback.
abstract: We study an online reusable resource allocation problem motivated by mobile edge AI platforms, where sequentially arriving requests must be immediately admitted and assigned to one of multiple edge service options with limited reusable capacities or offloaded to a remote central server. If accepted, a request occupies one service slot of the selected option for a random duration and yields a stochastic reward. The problem is particularly challenging because arrivals may be adversarial, reward and service-time statistics are both unknown and heterogeneous across request types and service options, and reward feedback can be delayed beyond service completion. To address these challenges, we propose an index-based online learning algorithm that combines optimistic reward estimates with a conservative, utilization-aware opportunity-cost penalty that captures the future value of reusable capacity. Using a primal-dual framework built on a novel reverse-order benchmark, we establish competitive-ratio guarantees under both bounded and light-tailed unbounded feedback delays. In particular, under a homogeneous reward-service model with i.i.d. inter-arrival times, our algorithm achieves an asymptotic competitive ratio of 1 - 1/e as reusable capacities grow large. Experimental results on a real-world dataset further demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

title: Joint Incentive Contract and Assignment Design for Mobile Networked Platforms with Endogenous Supply.
abstract: Mobile networked platforms such as crowdsensing markets, edge-computing exchanges, vehicular service systems, and sponsored-content programs must coordinate two coupled levers: an assignment rule that decides who serves each request and an incentive contract that determines how realized value is shared. In all four settings, supply is endogenous, that is, it depends on the platform's own decisions: providers remain active only when expected earnings cover their private participation cost. We study a discounted platform problem in which assignment and revenue sharing jointly shape future supply. We calibrate the tractable one-period objective using an auxiliary memoryless discounted surrogate: it maximizes a global lower bound on that surrogate objective, and near high-survival stationary operating points its retention coefficient becomes the local shadow price of discounted future welfare within the surrogate model. This yields an Equimarginal Principle requiring efficient platforms to equalize the marginal retention efficiency of assignment and contracting. Under complete information, we obtain an urgency-adjusted assignment score, a KKT condition for the contract, and a Frank-Wolfe coordinate-ascent benchmark with an O(t/K) joint stationarity rate. Under hidden provider quality, we develop SE-RW-UCB, a subsidized-exploration algorithm with retention-weighted contextual assignment and a learned safe contract floor. A KuaiRec-based online recommendation benchmark shows that separated designs leave a sizable retention gap. In that benchmark, Oracle Fixed is the profit leader, whereas SE-RW-UCB attains the strongest high-type and all-provider retention at an interior contract. The service-quality differences are comparatively small, indicating that the main leverage of co-design in this calibration lies in supply preservation rather than per-request quality gains.

title: LLM-Enabled Self-Organizing UAV Networks for Autonomous Service Provisioning.
abstract: The growing demand for flexible and resilient low-altitude connectivity is driving UAV networks toward increasingly autonomous operation. However, existing approaches often assume known user distributions, fixed network configurations, or treat exploration, access, and backhaul separately, resulting in a gap between user discovery and end-to-end service in initially unknown environments. To address this challenge, we propose a self-organizing heterogeneous UAV networking framework, referred to as Discovery-to-Service (D2S) Network, that supports the complete process from user discovery to end-to-end service provisioning. The framework adopts a dual-timescale coordination mechanism: at the fast timescale, onboard graph reinforcement learning agents perform user exploration and local control, while at the slower timescale, a basestation-hosted LLM reconfigures the access and backhaul infrastructure based on discovered demands and the global network state. Experiments over 42 scenarios show that, compared with a heuristic connectivity-constrained grid-greedy method, the proposed framework improves effective coverage by 23.38 percentage points, terminal throughput by 55.3%, and cumulative throughput by 44.3%, demonstrating its effectiveness for autonomous network formation under unknown demand.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Pushing Bistatic Wireless Sensing toward High Accuracy at the Sub-Wavelength Scale.
abstract: Contactless sensing using wireless communication signals has garnered significant attention due to its non-intrusive nature and ubiquitous infrastructure. Despite the promise, the inherent bistatic deployment of wireless communication introduces clock asynchronism, which leads to unknown phase offsets in channel response and hinders fine-grained sensing. State-of-the-art systems widely adopt the cross-antenna channel response ratio to cancel these detrimental phase offsets. However, the channel response ratio preserves sensing feature accuracy only at integer-wavelength target displacements, losing sub-wavelength fidelity. To overcome this limitation, we derive the first quantitative mapping between the distorted ratio feature and the ideal-channel sensing feature. Building on this foundation, we develop a robust framework that leverages raw channel response amplitude to recover the ideal sensing feature from the distorted ratio. Real-world experiments across Wi-Fi and LoRa signals demonstrate that our method can effectively reconstruct sub-wavelength displacement details, achieving nearly an order-of-magnitude improvement in accuracy.

title: Age of Information for Real-Time Radio Map Monitoring.
abstract: In this paper, we propose radio map age of information (RM-AOI), a new metric for measuring the information freshness of a reconstructed radio map. Specifically, we consider a radio map monitoring system in which sensors transmit spectrum measurement packets to a central monitoring station for radio map reconstruction. To reflect the contributions of measurements to radio map reconstruction, we define RM-AOI by weighting each sensor's age of information (AoI). We model packet generation and transmission as a homogeneous multi-source M/M/1 first-come-first-served (FCFS) queue. Under this model, we develop an analytical framework based on time reversal and joint workload analysis to derive exact expressions for the time average and temporal variance of RM-AOI. Simulations validate the exact expressions, demonstrate how queue parameters affect RM-AOI, and show that the mean squared error (MSE) of radio map reconstruction generally increases with both metrics.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: TrustSense: Structure-Adaptive Trust Inference for Resilient Cooperative IoT Sensing.
abstract: Cooperative IoT sensing must assess reports from noisy, faulty, or compromised devices despite churn and changing inter-device relationships. We present TrustSense, a structure-adaptive GNN framework for per-report trust evaluation. TrustSense represents active devices as a dynamic graph and maps each report's neighborhood-based reconstruction residual to a trust score. A layer-wise soft edge mask downweights less informative dependencies, while forced anchor attention reserves a controlled share of attention for available trusted anchors. At runtime, historical consistency drives anchor-rooted credit diffusion to prioritize returning devices, and accepted reports guide subsequent evaluations. Shared GNN parameters make TrustSense inductive, enabling targeted adaptation to unseen devices without usable history. TrustSense is also location-centric, device-agnostic, and prior-free with respect to the sensing process, assuming neither a parametric sensing-value distribution nor a known propagation model. We evaluate TrustSense on synthetic RF data and real LoED traces with injected attacks. With 10% additive-bias attackers on LoED, it improves F1 by 4.25× over the strongest evaluated baseline and achieves a lower Brier score. These gains persist with up to 50% malicious devices, while inference latency remains within 230-250 ms at several thousand devices.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: PQ-FL-IDS: A Post Quantum Safe Federated Edge Intrusion Detection Scheme underlying 6G.
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables Intrusion Detection System (IDS) models to be trained across Sixth Generation (6G) edge nodes without transferring sensitive traffic records to a central server. However, the model updates exchanged during FL-based IDS (FL-IDS) training remain exposed to interception and harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks by quantum-capable adversaries. This paper presents PQ-FL-IDS, a post-quantum (PQ) FL-IDS scheme for 6G edge networks. It protects model-update exchange using a real, non-simulated Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM-512, NIST FIPS 203), the Advanced Encryption Standard in Galois/Counter Mode with a 256-bit key (AES-256-GCM), and per-round forward secrecy through ephemeral key pairs. Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD) with Rényi DP accounting further bounds record-level leakage from local updates. In each round, clients train locally with calibrated DP noise, encrypt the model update, and send only the protected payload for server-side aggregation. We evaluate PQ-FL-IDS on ToN-IoT with a 1D-CNN and FedAvg, and on CICIoT2023 with MobileNetV2-1D and FedProx, under baseline, PQC-only, and PQC+DP settings. ML-KEM-512 with AES-256-GCM adds less than 0.003% computational overhead relative to per-round training time and at most 3.5 KB of payload expansion, with no accuracy loss, and remains stable from 2 to 5 clients. The privacy analysis shows predictable ε growth with the subsampling rate and characterizes the privacy-utility frontier: formal budgets of ε = 0.9-2.4 are obtained for σ = 0.8-1.1, with a utility cost that depends strongly on task complexity.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: TWINERGY: Digital Twin Empowered Practical Energy Saving in Heterogeneous Mobile Networks.
abstract: Energy consumption has become a pressing concern as mobile networks expand rapidly, with the radio access network accounting for the dominant share. Among energy-saving techniques, cell shutdown offers large saving potential: it selectively switches off capacity cells in heterogeneous networks while a coverage layer preserves service. However, optimizing cell shutdown policies faces two key challenges: (i) live trial-and-error is prohibitively risky, while traditional simulators cannot capture the complex dynamics needed for reliable evaluation; (ii) operator-deployed threshold policies are interpretable but hard to optimize at scale. On the other hand, binary status optimization is more tractable but produces policies incompatible with operator workflows. We propose Twinergy, a digital twin-empowered framework for practical cell shutdown at scale. Twinergy builds a Network Digital Twin for safe virtual evaluation, and decouples policy design into two stages: first optimizing binary on/off decisions under QoS constraints, and then mapping them into deployable thresholds, with a dedicated module for each. For scalable decision optimization, we design Cable, a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework with shared policies, causal graph-based spatio-temporal encoding, and credit-guided cooperative learning. For threshold synthesis, we design a differentiable mapping module that introduces SoftControl as a surrogate for hard dual-threshold logic, enabling thresholds to be calibrated in continuous space via stable supervised optimization. Experiments on a digital twin built from 14,349 real-world base stations and deployments across three commercial trial networks with over 3,400 cells show that Twinergy achieves up to 26.0% and 12.4% energy savings in 4G and 5G digital-twin evaluation, respectively, and delivers up to 13.07% and 12.20% energy-efficiency improvements in rural and dense 5G live networks without degrading QoS.

title: FedCRA: Client Risk-aware Aggregation via Update Reconstruction for IoT-based Federated Learning.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables distributed model training without sharing raw data, making it particularly suitable for Internet of Things (IoT) environments. However, FL remains vulnerable to poisoning attacks, where malicious clients manipulate local updates to corrupt global model optimization. Existing defenses mainly focus on updates within a single round and may confuse heterogeneous benign updates with malicious ones. In this paper, we propose FedCRA, a client risk-aware aggregation framework that exploits historical trajectories and trusted reference updates to reconstruct updates. Furthermore, the risk-aware aggregation jointly considers reconstruction gap, reference gap, and historical trajectory information to adaptively suppress suspicious updates. Extensive experiments under multiple poisoning attacks and heterogeneous data distributions demonstrate that FedCRA achieves stronger robustness than several representative aggregation methods while maintaining good scalability in large-scale FL.

title: Poster: Jamming-Resilient FR3 5G NR via Adaptive Sensing and Covariance-Based RX Null-Forming.
abstract: We present work in progress on interference rejection at a software-defined 5G NR gNB through receive-side null-forming, where the spatial covariance matrix used to compute the null-forming weights is estimated exclusively from transmission-free windows, with neither gNB nor UE signals present. Silent sensing opportunities arise during light DL traffic or are explicitly reserved within the TDD pattern. A power detector on the gNB's own receive chain identifies these windows in real time from ADC energy, allowing the FPGA to select exactly the samples that are free of the gNB's own transmission for covariance estimation. The resulting null-forming weights suppress an interferer without attenuating the desired uplink. The system is implemented on an Open Air Interface (OAI) 5G NR standalone testbed with an FPGA/RFSoC-based FR3 multi-antenna front-end and a software-defined incumbent/jammer emulator.

verified_metadata.abstract: We present work in progress on interference rejection at a software-defined 5G NR gNB through receive-side null-forming, where the spatial covariance matrix used to compute the null-forming weights is estimated exclusively from transmission-free windows, with neither gNB nor UE signals present. Silent sensing opportunities arise during light DL traffic or are explicitly reserved within the TDD pattern. A power detector on the gNB's own receive chain identifies these windows in real time from ADC energy, allowing the FPGA to select exactly the samples that are free of the gNB's own transmission for covariance estimation. The resulting null-forming weights suppress an interferer without attenuating the desired uplink. The system is implemented on an Open Air Interface (OAI) 5G NR standalone testbed with an FPGA/RFSoC-based FR3 multi-antenna front-end and a software-defined incumbent/jammer emulator.

title: C-MoA-XRT: Explainability-Aware Trust Routing for Collaborative Threat Detection in Mobile-Edge Networks.
abstract: Threat detection in mobile-edge networks requires reliable inference from heterogeneous telemetry whose availability and evidential quality may vary over time. LLM-assisted detectors further introduce uncertainty because prediction confidence may not reflect evidence trustworthiness, while collaborative reasoning can amplify unsupported decisions. This paper proposes C-MoA-XRT, a trust-aware collaborative Mixture-of-Agents framework for resilient mobile-edge threat detection. C-MoA-XRT distributes complementary network evidence across specialized LLM agents and performs event-specific trust routing before collaborative inference. The proposed routing mechanism separates prediction confidence from decision authority by assessing the reliability, consistency, and evidential support of each specialist output. A defensive red-team reasoning stage subsequently examines the fused evidence, while an evidence-anchored decision firewall constrains unstable collaborative reasoning from overriding the calibrated detection outcome. Experiments on NF-UNSW-NB15 show that C-MoA-XRT achieves an F1 score of 0.900 with full attack recall and reduces the false-positive rate by approximately 75% relative to the evaluated single-agent RAG+LLM baseline. Under measurement drift, trust-aware evidence gating improves PR-AUC from 0.694 to 0.917 over confidence-based routing, while maintaining resilience under the evaluated telemetry-dropout and unreliable-specialist conditions. These results demonstrate that explicit control of evidence trust and reasoning authority can improve the robustness of collaborative LLM-based threat detection in mobile-edge networks.

title: Optimizing Stochastic Gradient Push under Broadcast Communications.
abstract: We consider the problem of minimizing the convergence time for decentralized federated learning (DFL) in wireless networks under broadcast communications, with focus on mixing matrix design. The mixing matrix is a critical hyperparameter for DFL that simultaneously controls the convergence rate across iterations and the communication demand per iteration, both strongly influencing the convergence time. Although the problem has been studied previously, existing solutions are mostly designed for decentralized parallel stochastic gradient descent (D-PSGD), which requires the mixing matrix to be symmetric and doubly stochastic. These constraints confine the activated communication graph to undirected (i.e., bidirected) graphs, which limits design flexibility. In contrast, we consider mixing matrix design for stochastic gradient push (SGP), which allows asymmetric mixing matrices and hence directed communication graphs. By analyzing how the convergence rate of SGP depends on the mixing matrices, we extract an objective function that explicitly depends on graph-theoretic parameters of the activated communication graph, based on which we develop an efficient design algorithm with performance guarantees. Our evaluations based on real data show that the proposed solution can notably reduce the convergence time compared to the state of the art without compromising the quality of the trained model.

title: FEdgeNAV: Edge-Based Federated Learning Framework for Wheel Odometry Fault Detection in Industrial AGV Fleet Navigation.
abstract: Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) rely on accurate wheel odometry for reliable navigation; however, wheel slip and varying terrain conditions introduce positioning errors that degrade navigation performance. This paper presents FEdgeNAV, a lightweight edge-based federated learning framework for collaborative wheel odometry fault detection in heterogeneous industrial environments. The proposed framework employs a lightweight 1D CNN-GRU model trained collaboratively across distributed edge clients using Federated Averaging (FedAvg), while keeping raw navigation data local by exchanging only model parameters. Wheel odometry faults are identified through residual analysis between the estimated and measured vehicle speeds. Experimental evaluation on the NavINST dataset demonstrated accurate vehicle-speed estimation and residual-based wheel-odometry fault detection across heterogeneous operating conditions. Furthermore, the proposed framework achieved computationally efficient inference on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, demonstrating its suitability for real-time deployment on resource-constrained edge platforms for industrial AGVs.

title: Foundation Model-Aided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Wireless Random Access Network Optimization.
abstract: Random access (RA) is one of the most foundational medium access control (MAC) layer scheduling schemes for handling unpredictable data traffic from multiple terminals. While multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has been explored to optimize RA-based wireless networks, its reliance on experience-driven, distributed policy learning incurs significant training overhead for each optimization task, limiting its feasibility in real-world applications. In this work, we propose to leverage a foundation model (FM) to improve MARL efficiency across diverse RA network optimization tasks. Specifically, we design an FM-aided actor-critic algorithm within a consensus-based decentralized MARL architecture and provide its convergence analysis under local reward exchanges and nonlinear value function approximations to show that our algorithm achieves the same convergence order as the conventional MARL with critic model exchanges and linear approximations. Our numerical results show that our FM-based approach significantly enhances MARL speed for RA network optimization.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Towards Agile and Active Scene Update for Embodied Space Exploration: A WiFi-Guided Approach.
abstract: Timely scene updating is essential for embodied agents operating in dynamic indoor environments. While cameras and LiDAR are effective for high-fidelity reconstruction and verification, relying on them alone for long-term maintenance is costly, since robots must repeatedly revisit large areas to rediscover relatively sparse changes. This paper presents WiDR, a WiFi-guided framework for efficient and active scene updating. The key idea is to use ubiquitous wireless signals as a low-overhead prior indicating where meaningful changes are likely to occur, thereby guiding visual or depth-based verification, rather than using wireless sensing to reconstruct the scene itself. WiDR integrates wireless priors with floorplan context to build a belief-aware navigation graph, and formulates scene updating as a budget-constrained utility maximization problem that jointly considers navigation, sensing, updating, and model refinement. To remain effective in long-term dynamic environments, WiDR further incorporates active refinement using robot-verified observations to improve its change prediction quality. Experimental results in a three-room indoor testbed show that WiDR achieves higher update utility under the same budget by directing sensing effort toward high-value regions instead of relying on coverage-driven or vision-only exploration.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Prism: Communication-efficient Distributed Inference for Foundation Models at Edge.
abstract: Foundation models (FMs) achieved remarkable success across vision and language tasks but pose significant challenges for deployment at the edge devices. This motivates the need for practical and efficient strategies for distributed inference at the edge. In this work, we propose Prism, a communication-efficient and compute-aware strategy for distributed Transformer inference. Prism leverages a Segment Means representation to approximate intermediate features, substantially reducing inter-device communication. Additionally, we restructure the self-attention to eliminate redundant computations caused by per-device Key/Value calculation in position-wise partitioning and design a partition-aware causal masking scheme tailored for autoregressive models. We evaluate Prism on ViT, BERT, and GPT-2 across diverse datasets, namely CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k, GLUE, and CBT. Our results demonstrate substantial reductions in communication overhead (up to 99.2% for BERT at compression rate CR = 128) and per-device computation (51.24% for BERT at the same setting), with only minor accuracy degradation. This method offers a scalable and practical solution for deploying foundation models in distributed resource-constrained environments.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: MIRA: An Edge-Cloud Multimodal LLM Framework for DESH Assessment in IoT-Enabled MRI Workflows.
abstract: Connected MRI scanners operate as networked medical devices within DICOM-based healthcare Internet of Things (IoT) workflows, but conventional connectivity primarily moves images to a Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) rather than adding task-specific reasoning near acquisition. Building on DESH-App 2.0, a preceding machine-learning contribution accepted for oral presentation at SIN Firenze 2026, this paper specifies MIRA (Multimodal Imaging Reasoning and Assessment), a vendor-neutral edge-cloud module for assessing disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid spaces (DESH). A hospital-edge gateway validates and de-identifies 3D T1-weighted DICOM studies, derives ventricular, high-convexity, and Sylvian-fissure masks with SegFormer3D, and converts each volume into a compact evidence package comprising 12 representative slices with overlays, 17 global, zonal, and ratio features, and quality-control tokens. LLaVA-Med-7B and Lingshu-7B are adapted through 4-bit QLoRA to return constrained JSON containing class, confidence, named anatomical evidence, and an abstention or quality warning. The edge-cloud partition keeps raw volumes inside the institutional network; only the compact evidence package may reach an authenticated inference service, while structured outputs return to the PACS workstation. The evaluation protocol jointly covers diagnostic discrimination, calibration, evidence agreement, unsupported claims, abstention, latency, transmitted bytes, memory demand, link-loss recovery, and multi-device interoperability. MIRA is designed to add auditable multimodal reasoning to connected MRI workflows without modifying safety-critical scanner controls.

title: An Agentic AI Architecture for Zero-Touch IoT Device Onboarding and Interoperability.
abstract: The heterogeneity of Internet of Things (IoT) devices remains a major barrier to scalable deployment, automated onboarding, and cross-platform interoperability. Device-specific protocols, software dependencies, telemetry formats, and runtime constraints often require manual configuration and ad-hoc integration logic. This paper proposes an agentic AI architecture for zero-touch IoT device onboarding, where a large language model is used as an autonomous configuration agent capable of generating device-side software, installing dependencies, validating runtime behavior, and recursively correcting failures until convergence is achieved. The proposed architecture introduces a closed-loop workflow that combines device inspection, AI-based runtime generation, remote deployment, telemetry validation, and self-correction. Interoperability is addressed through a normalized telemetry contract that abstracts device-specific behavior into a common telemetry representation. We evaluate the approach on a real IoT device by benchmarking multiple AI models under clean installation conditions in two campaigns: the original pipeline and a second pipeline assisted by a locally trained semantic context optimizer. The comparison covers convergence time, correction cycles, recursive iterations, and prompt tokens. The optimizer-assisted campaign reduced prompt redundancy and recursive recovery effort while preserving successful onboarding across all tested models. Overall, the results show that agentic AI can support zero-touch onboarding while exposing measurable differences among models in reliability, efficiency, and runtime convergence.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Routing and Topology Design for Low Earth Orbit Satellite Networks under Demand Uncertainty.
abstract: We study the space segment of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks that support satellite-to-satellite communication via inter-satellite links (ISLs). Our goal is to jointly design topologies and routing strategies that are robust to uncertain traffic demand. Leveraging the regularity and symmetry inherent in LEO constellations, we analyze traffic-oblivious routing schemes that exploit this structure. We show that Valiant Load Balancing (VLB) is optimal for symmetric networks in minimizing worst-case congestion. On the topology side, we demonstrate that minimizing average shortest path length (ASPL) leads to asymptotically optimal performance as the network scales. We introduce a new class of symmetric and uniform topologies, called 2-color topologies, which outperform conventional grid-based designs in terms of worst-case congestion and ASPL. In particular, we prove that 2-color topologies admit an ASPL lower bound scaling of Θ(N3), whereas traditional grid-based topologies have an ASPL lower bound of Θ(N) for a network of N nodes. We validate these performance gains on a realistic-scale LEO constellation with practical link range constraints.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Poster: Wideband RFI Control using Digital Interferer/Jammer Extraction and Analog Subtraction.
abstract: High-power jamming/RFI in out-of-band spectrum can cause receiver nonlinearity and reduced ADC dynamic range in sensitive RF receivers. Radio frequency interference (RFI) is typically distributed in clumps across the spectrum, and signals of interest are interspaced with RFI in the frequency domain. Although analog passive filters can suppress known RFI bands, the frequency spectrum of RFI is not fixed and needs real-time reconfiguration. This work proposes an analog cancellation scheme in which clean copies of bandpass RFI components are selectively enhanced in the digital domain and applied in analog for real-time cancellation across wide bandwidths. This poster presents a reconfigurable FIR digital filter for real-time RFI cancellation implemented on an RF-SoC platform. The filter employs a polyphase systolic array matrix-vector multiplication (MVM) engine, with adaptive coefficients dynamically loaded to suppress narrowband and broadband interference. The extracted RFI signal is converted through a DAC and subtracted from the antenna input in the analog domain. For a single-tone interferer at 151.25 MHz, 34.4 dB of real-time RFI cancellation was achieved within a 1 GHz instantaneous receiver bandwidth, reducing the RFI-driven headroom requirement at the second ADC by 34.4 dB, potentially allowing increased downstream gain and improved utilization of the ADC dynamic range.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: OAM-Enabled Multi-User Uplink for Sub-THz Networks.
abstract: The sub-THz frequency band offers significant potential to increase wireless capacity, providing the capability to accommodate growing network demands. Multi-user uplink further improves spectral efficiency, enabling high-throughput communication from multiple users to a common access point. In this work, we propose Multiuser OAM Uplink for Sub-THz (MOUST), a sub-THz multi-user communication framework that leverages orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) multiplexing to enable high-rate communications. To adapt orthogonal, broadside OAM systems for multi-user reception, we perform receive beam-steering for each user and embed each singleuser phase profile into a multi-user receive aperture. We validate the proposed approach using two sub-THz experimental testbeds: one to characterize the amplitude and phase profiles across a wide bandwidth, and another to evaluate achievable data rates and multiuser gains. From these results, we perform extensive analysis and observe an average 1.75x multi-user sum-rate gain compared to single-user transmission for two users. This provides insight into practical design trade-offs and quantifies the multi-user multiplexing capabilities of MOUST.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: BrewSense: A Mobile Water Quality Monitoring Platform using Laser Reflection near Brewster Angle.
abstract: BrewSense is a mobile water-quality monitoring platform for realtime, large-scale detection of inland water pollution beyond the reach of grab sampling and remote sensing, whose alternatives are invasive, expensive, or limited to narrow classes of solutes and controlled environments. BrewSense leverages laser reflection near Brewster's angle to remotely infer the refractive index of surface water, which varies approximately linearly with the concentration of both ionic and organic solutes. It combines a beam-splitter and orthogonal-polarizer front-end that strongly suppresses ambient light, synchronized electrodynamic indexers with magnetic angle sensing, and hierarchical angular sampling, Gaussian spot filtering, and derivative-based Brewster-angle fitting that stabilize measurements under platform motion, waves, turbidity, and temperature variations. Implemented on a UAV, BrewSense operates at meter-scale standoff distances and achieves sub-10-4 refractive-index resolution under controlled conditions. Controlled and real-lake-water tank experiments evaluate inorganic salts (NaCl, NH4Cl) and organic solutes (glucose, urea), and a UAV deployment validates end-to-end operation in a NaCl-dominated field setting. BrewSense achieves up to 3.2× lower error than prior UWB and vibration-based systems and an approximately 8% mean relative concentration-estimation error across 20 UAV field sites.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Online Joint Pricing and Scheduling in Distributed Networked Platforms.
abstract: In distributed networked platforms, such as geographically distributed data centers and electric vehicle charging networks, there are multiple resource providers that can serve user requests arriving sequentially over time. In this paper, we study an online posted pricing problem jointly with scheduling in distributed networked platforms. In such systems, user requests arrive sequentially over time, and each request (if accepted) can be served by one of multiple resource providers. Rather than centrally assigning a provider, the platform posts prices together with corresponding scheduling decisions for all providers, and each user independently selects one option or leaves based on the posted prices and its private valuation. As demand increases, posted pricing and scheduling act as complementary mechanisms for regulating system usage. However, designing effective online posted pricing policies is challenging because of uncertainty in arrivals and the intertemporal coupling across requests, where current pricing decisions affect future feasibility and performance. We propose a class of parameterized threshold-based posted pricing policies that enable tractable online decision-making with provable performance guarantees. We identify a sufficient condition that ensures feasibility and supports competitive analysis, which in turn characterizes a structured policy design space. Building on this structure, we develop a learning-based approach to improve empirical performance under realistic demand patterns. We evaluate our approach on the problem of pricing and scheduling in electric vehicle charging stations using real-world charging traces, and demonstrate that the empirical performance of our algorithm outperforms other benchmark algorithms.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Rethinking Passive RIS at Sub-6 GHz: A Reality Check on Practical Gains.
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) promise low-power link enhancement through programmable reflections, yet their value at sub-6 GHz, where direct paths and rich multipath already exist, remains unclear. We combine Sionna ray tracing with indoor and outdoor over-the-air measurements of a 2 × 2 MIMO-OFDM system using a 144-element dual-polarized, near-passive prototype with a 25λ2 aperture and approximately 175 mW of control-plane power. Even at radiative-near-field separations favorable to the cascaded link budget, gains remain highly conditional: directional illumination improves the weaker mode by up to 11 dB indoors over no reflector, but primarily strengthens the dominant mode by 6-8 dB outdoors over a matched metal reflector. Under low-gain monopole illumination, the RIS does not consistently improve the weaker mode and can degrade it by up to about 5 dB. Thus, compact near-passive RIS is not broadly beneficial; its gains depend critically on the incident power at the RIS and the propagation environment.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Semantic-Aware Scheduling for Task-Oriented Communication by Mitigating Congestion in Emergency Networks.
abstract: Modern communication systems have fundamentally relied on bit-level perfect transmission, which becomes critically inefficient in resource-constrained disaster scenarios where bandwidth is scarce and timely information is paramount. The convergence of sensing, artificial intelligence, and communication is emerging as a key paradigm for next-generation networks, where semantic communication, transmitting the contextual meaning of data rather than raw bits, offers a promising solution. However, existing semantic approaches lack the integration of emergency-critical semantic extraction from visual sensors with semantic-aware network resource allocation. This paper bridges this gap by proposing a novel end-to-end semantic communication framework for congested emergency networks. We develop a task-oriented image captioning pipeline that fine-tunes a BLIP model on a custom-built dataset annotated with emergency-critical captions to convert sensed images into concise, actionable textual descriptions. Furthermore, we design a suite of semantic-aware MAC schedulers (specifically, DRR-Sorted, DRR-Boosted, DRR-Hybrid, and PF-Priority) that utilize content-derived priority tags to intelligently allocate network resources and mitigate congestion. Integrated into an OMNeT++/Simu5G simulation of a 5G mmWave network with a constrained backhaul, our framework delivers emergency information over 98% faster than traditional image transmission. This represents a paradigm shift from multi-second delays to near-instantaneous delivery of life-saving intelligence for first responders, demonstrating the practical benefits of tightly integrated sensing, AI, and communication pipelines.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Physics-Informed Kernelized Thompson Sampling for Beam Management in Millimeter-Wave Systems.
abstract: Maintaining connectivity in directional millimeter-wave communications requires frequent beam probing and realignment, incurring substantial overhead. We address this challenge by formulating beam tracking as a kernelized multi-armed bandit over the two-dimensional beam-angle domain. We propose GP-TSAF, a Gaussian process Thompson sampling algorithm with a physics-informed array-factor (AF) kernel. Derived directly from the known array geometry and beam codebook, the AF kernel captures beam-pattern overlap, including sidelobe interactions and null-induced decorrelation, without learning the beam-correlation structure from data. This allows each received signal strength (RSS) observation to update the posterior over the full codebook, enabling data-efficient tracking under limited measurements. To improve robustness under mobility, we further introduce adaptive correlation scaling, which weakens cross-beam smoothing as the prediction error increases without requiring an explicit mobility model. For a stationary fixed-kernel variant, we establish a cumulative-regret bound whose kernel-dependent complexity is characterized by the AF-kernel spectrum. Evaluation on 30 GHz simulation datasets with 32- and 64-beam codebooks and a 28 GHz over-the-air dataset with a 28-beam codebook shows that GP-TSAF achieves lower mean oracle gap and cumulative regret than several baselines.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Continuous Passive Target Tracking over Intermittent and Narrow Sensing Beams in 6G Networks.
abstract: 6G networks promise an advanced infrastructure for high-precision passive sensing and tracking, particularly in emerging sectors like Low-Altitude Economy (LAE) and Internet of Vehicles. However, realizing passive sensing in 6G remains challenging due to its unique signal characteristics, especially the extreme directionality of narrow beams and the intermittent availability of sensing resources, which are subordinated to the primary communication traffic. In this paper, we propose SPOT, a novel passive beam tracking framework that achieves continuous, high-precision tracking using only temporally sparse sensing slots. We employ an Interacting Multiple Model combined with an Extended Kalman Filter (IMM-EKF) to robustly predict non-linear target dynamics. We further develop a beam selection strategy that maximizes Fisher information gain to minimize tracking uncertainty, integrated with an opportunistic exploration mechanism to detect emerging targets. To reduce computation complexity, we introduce a lightweight approximation of the Posterior Cramér-Rao Lower Bound. Extensive evaluations using both simulations and real-world datasets demonstrate that SPOT significantly outperforms existing baselines, achieving a detection rate near 100% and an average tracking error below 1 meter, even in multi-target scenarios with highly sparse temporal updates.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Serving Chain-structured Jobs with Large Memory Footprints with Application to Large Foundation Model Serving.
abstract: As a current trend in Artificial Intelligence (AI), large foundation models are increasingly employed as the core of AI services. However, even after training, serving such models at scale remains a challenging task due to their heavy resource footprints, particularly in terms of GPU memory. While recent works revealed unique characteristics of systems serving foundation models that distinguish them from traditional distributed computing systems, there is still a lack of fundamental understanding of the underlying system management problems. This work aims at addressing this gap by extracting a novel problem of “server chain composition” via block placement and cache allocation for serving chain-structured jobs with large memory footprints, which models a fundamental problem in serving large foundation models through pipeline parallelism. After showing the NP-hardness of the optimal solution, the focus is turned to developing scalable algorithms with guaranteed performance under state-of-the-art load balancing. Application of the proposed solution to a distributed large language model (LLM) serving system shows significant reduction of response times compared to state-of-the-art solutions.

title: Shear: Goal-Oriented Anomaly Detection on Compressed Time Series via Semantic Transition Graph.
abstract: Sensor data in IoT systems are commonly compressed to meet resource constraints, yet anomaly detection directly on compressed data remains largely unexplored. This challenge is particularly evident for recurrent anomalies, which commonly appear as repeated abnormal patterns in long-running IoT streams. Existing approaches often become cumbersome or expensive since they decouple compression from analytics, requiring detection to reprocess full raw data, while supervised deep learning alternatives further demand labels or incur computational overhead unsuitable for edge deployment. In this paper, we propose Shear, a goal-oriented unsupervised method via Semantic Transition Graph (STG) induced directly from compressed time series. The STG organizes compressed representation as semantic states and encodes their temporal transitions, so that recurrent anomaly patterns are identified through unlikely state transition chains without decompression or neural network inference. Experiments on public datasets show that Shear achieves better detection performance than state-of-the-art approaches, while running 3.9× to 11.2× faster than subsequence-oriented methods and up to 2219× faster than deep learning baselines, with substantially reduced storage and memory footprint.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Resource-Constrained Semantic-Aware Remote Estimation with Overlapping Sensor Coverage.
abstract: We study semantic-aware remote estimation of multiple finite-state Markov sources observed by K sensors with overlapping coverage. The sensors share a time-division multiple-access uplink and differ in transmission reliability, delivery delay, and transmission budget. In each slot, the scheduler jointly selects a source and one of its monitoring sensors, or remains idle, to minimize the long-run average cost of actuation error subject to global and per-sensor transmission-frequency constraints. We formulate this problem as a finite average-cost constrained Markov decision process. We show that the transmission resource functions have rank at most K. Consequently, the Lagrangian depends only on K effective transmission costs, and an optimal constrained solution can be represented using at most K +1 deterministic policy-recurrent-class components. We further characterize the piecewise-affine concave Lagrangian value function and derive projected dual subgradient ascent over an explicitly bounded multiplier set. Numerical results illustrate the value-function structure, the need for policy randomization in a representative instance, and the interaction between global and per-sensor transmission budgets.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Wait to be Fresh: Optimal Sampling for Asymmetric Multi-Source Status Updates under Probabilistic Scheduling.
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the exact age-optimal sampling policy for an asymmetric multi-source status update system operating under a probabilistic scheduler. Our objective is to minimize the long-term average weighted AoI when transmitting packets of varying importance over asymmetric channels with distinct random delay distributions, for any given probabilistic scheduler. We rigorously prove that the optimal sampling policy follows a strict threshold structure, providing the first exact closed-form system of equations to determine these optimal thresholds for asymmetric sources. Crucially, our theoretical analysis reveals that the relative sizing of these thresholds is strictly governed by the ratio of a source's weight to its scheduling probability, completely decoupled from highly asymmetric channel delay distributions. Numerical evaluations demonstrate that our proposed policy consistently outperforms existing baseline schemes, particularly under extreme asymmetric network conditions.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Your Palm Is in My Hand: Palm-Vein Biometric Spoofing via Electromagnetic Side Channel.
abstract: As a biometric modality, palm-vein authentication has seen growing adoption in recent years and is becoming prevalent in wallet-free payments and critical access-control applications. Although palm-vein patterns are widely regarded as nearly impossible to forge or steal, our study reveals that electromagnetic emanations induced during sensor operation can leak information correlated with a user's palm-vein characteristics, enabling attackers to reconstruct palm-vein images and spoof authentication systems. In this paper, we present PVSpy, a novel attack framework that demonstrates the feasibility of this attack. Specifically, PVSpy passively captures electromagnetic emanations radiated from palm-vein sensors, extracts features that map the captured signals to palm-vein images, and exploits diffusion models for biometric reconstructions to spoof palm-vein authentication devices. We extensively evaluate PVSpy on five commercial devices, and the recovered vein patterns exhibit a promising level of similarity. In addition, we conduct 30 end-to-end spoofing attacks against these commercial-off-the-shelf devices with different types of palm-vein sensors, and PVSpy achieves 26.7% (top-1) and 63.3% (top-3) success rates.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: From Prediction to Decision: Dynamic Maintenance Scheduling in Industrial Edge Computing via Federated DRL.
abstract: In industrial edge computing, numerous devices must operate continuously to support time-critical services. Their degradation can lead to localized failures and reduce overall system uptime, making proactive maintenance necessary. Existing data-driven maintenance methods typically predict device health or remaining useful life using deep learning models and then trigger maintenance through predefined thresholds and heuristic rules. However, this open-loop paradigm cannot dynamically adapt its decisions to evolving conditions and struggles to scale maintenance intelligence across distributed edge sites, especially under data privacy constraints. This paper transitions from prediction to decision by reformulating maintenance scheduling as a closed-loop sequential decision-making problem. Specifically, we formulate a Long-Term Operational Cost Minimization (LTOCM) problem over three device operational modes to directly capture the trade-off between failure loss and maintenance cost. Based on LTOCM, we construct a Markov decision process with a cost-based reward and further introduce a degradation-aware reward to provide informative learning signals for maintenance timing. We then propose FDDM, a federated deep reinforcement learning scheme in which edge agents learn closed-loop maintenance policies locally and collaboratively improve them across distributed industrial edge sites without sharing raw operational data. Momentum-based global aggregation is further incorporated to stabilize federated policy learning. Extensive experiments on the NASA C-MAPSS dataset across multiple fault scenarios show that FDDM achieves near-optimal operational cost and faster convergence than representative baselines. Ablation and non-IID evaluations validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed design.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Poster: When Safer AI Makes the System Less Safe: Inference Reuse and Systemic Risk in Networked Autonomy.
abstract: Network-assisted inference can improve the decisions of autonomous agents, while reusing inference results can avoid repeated computation. However, when multiple agents reuse the same inference result, their failures become more coupled. We show that beyond a simple threshold, simultaneous failure can become more likely even though every agent is individually more accurate. We then characterize when the resource savings from reuse justify this added shared-failure risk.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: Demo: A Hybrid-Manufactured 3D-Printed Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface.
abstract: Practical research on Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces and H-MIMO surfaces requires low-cost, full-scale prototypes for testing their performance in real-world wireless links. However, conventional prototypes typically use expensive radio-frequency (RF) components and precisely manufactured printed circuit boards (PCBs) with stable dielectric properties to achieve a wide operating band and low reflection loss. Additive manufacturing (AM), or 3D printing, offers an attractive alternative by enabling rapid fabrication of low-cost RIS structures with geometries that are difficult to create using conventional PCB manufacturing techniques. This demo presents the first hybrid 3D-printed surface, which combines an inexpensive, standard FR-4 PCB carrying the control circuit with low-cost 3D-printed layers that provide a wide operating bandwidth. The demonstration includes OFDM transmission over the 4.6-5.35 GHz frequency range with a protective 3D-printed radome installed. In the geometry evaluated during the demo, the surface provides a received-power gain of up to 24 dB relative to the scenario without tge surface. The results show that hybrid fabrication based on low-cost AM and PCB technologies can be used to construct practical RIS testbeds for experimental wireless research.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing

title: FSMA: Scaling LoRa Satellite IoT with Link-aware Multiple Access.
abstract: Direct-to-satellite LoRa is rapidly becoming infrastructure for global IoT, but it faces a fundamental medium access control (MAC) bottleneck: a satellite's large footprint causes thousands of devices to collide on the same channel, while its motion induces rapid link variations, making link-unaware transmissions a persistent source of wasted airtime. These challenges demand random access solutions without requiring synchronization, handshakes, or an additional channel. However, ALOHA leaves collisions uncoordinated, and carrier sensing fails because devices across a footprint cannot hear each other. We propose Free Signal Multiple Access (FSMA), a gateway-controlled MAC protocol that works like a traffic light: the gateway sends a single LoRa upchirp (FreeChirp) only while the channel is idle, confining contention to a short sensing window, and at a lower spreading factor than the node uplink, implicitly deferring weak-link nodes through channel reciprocity, all without handshakes or hardware modifications. Hardware experiments with up to 25 off-the-shelf LoRa nodes and static and drone-mounted gateways demonstrate 2× higher throughput and 2.5-5× better packet reception ratio. Simulations with real satellite trajectories confirm scalability to 5000 devices per satellite pass, with up to 6.4× lower energy per successful packet.
conference_title: International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing
